preamble: Aspirated [kʰ] becomes voiced [g] mainly through Celtic initial mutations. In Welsh and Irish, word-initial voiceless stops are aspirated, so when a mutation turns /k/ into /g/ (Welsh soft mutation, Irish eclipsis), the result loses aspiration and gains voicing at once. The alternation is regular inside these morphologies, but it is rarely found as a sound change outside Celtic, because aspirated stops tend to resist voicing.

examples.note: Soft mutation of a feminine singular noun after the article; Welsh /k/ is set apart from /g/ mainly by aspiration.
Eclipsis; written gc and pronounced [g]. Irish voiceless stops are aspirated word-initially.
